translationRepairs: Empress Buluhan (Baiyuewu, granddaughter of the meritorious minister Puhua and daughter of Consort Telihusi; made empress at the start of Yuanzhen and invested in 1299; when Temür died in 1307 Külüg deposed her, exiled her to Dong'an, and soon had her executed. Though she dominated the inner court during Temür's late illnesses, she trusted the chief minister Harqasun and helped bring the Dade reign to a stable close—a point critics still acknowledged). Primary Consort Shilian Dali (Kongirat; died young; posthumously titled Empress Zhenci Jingyi in 1308 and enshrined at Chengzong's temple). Empress Qilijihutieni.

Empress Buluhan (Baiyuewu, granddaughter of the meritorious minister Puhua and daughter of the imperial son-in-law Telihusi; made empress at the start of Yuanzhen and invested in 1299; when Temür died in 1307 Külüg deposed her, exiled her to Dong'an, and soon had her executed. Though she dominated the inner court during Temür's late illnesses, she trusted the chief minister Harqasun and helped bring the Dade reign to a stable close—a point critics still acknowledged). Primary Consort Shilian Dali (Kongirat; died young; posthumously titled Empress Zhenci Jingyi in 1308 and enshrined at Chengzong's temple). Empress Qilijihutieni.
s0023 has 駙馬脫里忽思之女: 駙馬 is imperial son-in-law, not consort; the proposed phrasing corrects that mistranslation without other changes.

Chinese 阿納失舍里皇后 gives the name plainly; the square brackets are editorial scaffolding absent from the source and should be removed.
The cell is only 文宗; Toghun Temür wrongly names Huizong/Shundi, while Tuq Temür is the correct personal name for Wenzong under this chapter's emperor glosses.
Empress Anchuhan. Empress Yuelusha. Empress Buyanhudu. Empress Babusha. Empress Yesu. Empress Tuohusi. [Empress Maidi, titled Zhenyu Huish Sheng].
Empress Anchuhan. Empress Yuelusha. Empress Buyanhudu. Empress Babusha. Empress Yesu. Empress Tuohusi. Empress Maidi Zhenyu Huisheng.
邁來迪貞裕徽聖皇后 is one continuous title-name; removing brackets and joining 徽聖 as Huisheng restores that form.

Yesün Temür is a false conflation, but Xianzong is identifiable as Gammala from the Yuan History's imperial genealogy and biographies. The corrected parenthetical retains the useful personal identification.
Kamala is a false identification; the Yuan History's imperial genealogy and biographies identify Shunzong as Darmabala. The corrected parenthetical preserves that supported personal name.
